index.title: A Gray Line
index.prompt: The running example's vertical line is redrawn in mid-gray, with every pixel of its column at 0.5 instead of 1 and the background still 0. Work the network's forward pass for a line of brightness b and answer two questions: what probability does it give the class vertical at b = 0.5, and what brightness makes that probability exactly 0.9? 2 parts.
index.answer: Worked solutions are given part by part on the problem page. Attempt each part on paper before revealing it.

theory.title: A Gray Line
overview: The line is redrawn in mid-gray: every pixel of column 3 is 0.5 instead of 1, and the background stays 0. The filters, ReLU, pooling and the classification layer are the running example's, with weights of 0.25 on the four numbers of a class's own pooled map.

prompt.p: What probability does the network give "vertical"? Give it to three decimal places.

answer.p: Everything before the softmax scales with the image. A convolution multiplies pixels by weights and adds, so halving every pixel halves every value of both maps: each row of the vertical map becomes −1.5, 3, −1.5, 0, and the horizontal map stays 0. ReLU and the maximum of a block keep the factor, since $\max(0, 0.5x) = 0.5 \max(0, x)$. The pooled vertical map is 3, 0 in each row, its total is 6, and the scores are $0.25 \times 6 = 1.5$ and 0:

With two classes the softmax is $1 / (1 + e^{-(s_1 - s_2)})$, a function of the difference of the scores. Halving the image halved that difference, from 3 to 1.5, so the probability does not stay at 0.953, and it does not halve either.

prompt.p: How bright must the line be for the network to give "vertical" a probability of exactly 0.9? Give the pixel value to three decimal places.

answer.p: A line of brightness $b$ gives the scores $3b$ and 0, by the argument of Part 1. Then

about 187 on the 0 to 255 scale. Nothing in this network divides by the overall brightness, so its confidence measures how bright the line is as much as how vertical it is. A faint vertical line and a faint horizontal one both come out close to 0.5.
